The existing attained maximum and shifted-input guarantees are unchanged; connecting maximum, sum and normalization into one program remains outstanding despite the new separately verified components.
The new example component states its input domain, arithmetic order, storage and proof boundaries, fulfilling the existing example-level contract.
Finite real interpretations and all-result absolute errors are preserved; encoded signed zeros are not conflated with bitwise equality, and exponential and sum errors remain distinct.
The existing two-policy exponential allowance and encoded reciprocal provider are consumed unchanged; the new range proof retains all signed outcomes.
Specializing one row to exact unit weights, zero bias and no activation preserves the existing actual reduction program and its memory/execution contract, including redundant arithmetic.
The fetched normalization wrapper uses the existing rounded reciprocal relation and target policy, deriving finite output from the denominator guard without narrowing instruction semantics.
